purpose: Ponesimod is used to treat adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS). It helps reduce the number of flare-ups (relapses) and slows down the worsening of the disease. It is taken as a once-daily pill.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes mistakenly attacks your brain and spinal cord in MS. Ponesimod works by keeping certain immune cells (called lymphocytes) trapped inside your lymph nodes so they cannot travel to your brain and cause damage. Think of it like redirecting troublemakers away from the scene so they cannot cause harm.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include upper respiratory infections (like a cold), high blood pressure, slow heart rate (especially when you first start the medication), dizziness, tiredness, swelling in the arms or legs, and abnormal liver blood tests. You may also notice shortness of breath.
warnings: Important warnings: Your heart rate will be monitored for at least 4 hours when you take your first dose because this medicine can slow your heart. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as your MS symptoms could worsen quickly. This medicine weakens your immune system, so you are more likely to get infections — call your doctor if you have fever or signs of infection. It can also cause vision problems, liver problems, and harm an unborn baby, so tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Make sure your vaccinations are up to date before starting this medication.
typical_dosing: You start with a low dose and gradually increase it over 14 days (this is called a titration schedule) to help your body adjust and reduce heart-related side effects. After that, the maintenance dose is 20 mg taken by mouth once daily. Try to take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
